fanoutqa_002392.x:
Economy of Qatar :: Macro-economic trend :: part 01 :: chunk_0011
Qatar is now among the richest countries in the world, on a per person basis.[[39]](#cite_note-39) Current GDP per capita registered a world record-breaking peak growth of 1,156% in the 70s.[[40]](#cite_note-40) This became quickly unsustainable due to the [1980s oil glut](/wiki/1980s_oil_glut "1980s oil glut"), and Qatar's current GDP per capita contracted 53% in the 80s. But rising global oil demand helped current GDP per capita to expand 94% in the 90s. Despite efforts to promote the non-hydrocarbon sectors and diversify the economy from hydrocarbons to knowledge-based sectors, the oil and gas sector has consistently contributed to at least 80 percent of the government of Qatar’s total revenues since 2014, as well as 90 percent of Qatar’s total exports.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

In 2020 GDP PPP ~260 billion dollars.[[42]](#cite_note-42)

A very large ovarian cancer as seen on CT

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Serous_carcinoma_cytology.jpg/250px-Serous_carcinoma_cytology.jpg)](/wiki/File:Serous_carcinoma_cytology.jpg)

[Micrograph](/wiki/Micrograph "Micrograph") of [serous carcinoma](/wiki/Serous_carcinoma "Serous carcinoma"), a type of ovarian cancer, diagnosed in [peritoneal fluid](/wiki/Peritoneal_fluid "Peritoneal fluid")

Diagnosis of ovarian cancer starts with a physical examination (including a [pelvic examination](/wiki/Pelvic_examination "Pelvic examination")), a blood test (for [CA-125](/wiki/CA-125 "CA-125") and sometimes other markers), and [transvaginal ultrasound](/wiki/Transvaginal_ultrasound "Transvaginal ultrasound").[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)[[59]](#cite_note-59) Sometimes a [rectovaginal examination](/wiki/Rectovaginal_examination "Rectovaginal examination") is used to help plan a surgery.[[30]](#cite_note-Hoffman35-30) The diagnosis must be confirmed with surgery to inspect the [abdominal cavity](/wiki/Abdominal_cavity "Abdominal cavity"), take [biopsies](/wiki/Biopsies "Biopsies") (tissue samples for [microscopic analysis](/wiki/Histopathology "Histopathology")), and look for cancer cells in the abdominal fluid. This helps to determine if an ovarian mass is [benign](/wiki/Benign "Benign") or malignant.[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)

Ovarian cancer's early stages (I/II) are difficult to diagnose because most symptoms are nonspecific and thus of little use in diagnosis; as a result, it is rarely diagnosed until it spreads and advances to later stages (III/IV).[[60]](#cite_note-60) Additionally, symptoms of ovarian cancer may appear similar to [irritable bowel syndrome](/wiki/Irritable_bowel_syndrome "Irritable bowel syndrome"). Iggy Azalea has been nominated for numerous major music awards. Azalea was the first female and first non-American rapper to be featured on [*XXL*](/wiki/XXL_(magazine) "XXL (magazine)")'s "[Top 10 Freshman List](/wiki/XXL_(magazine)#Top_10_Freshmen "XXL (magazine)")".[[37]](#cite_note-freshman-37) In 2014, she received two [American Music Awards](/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2014 "American Music Awards of 2014") in the Rap/Hip-Hop categories, along with four more nominations, and one [MTV Video Music Award](/wiki/2014_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2014 MTV Video Music Awards") for her collaboration with Ariana Grande, along with seven more nominations, making her the most nominated artist at these respective award show editions.[[213]](#cite_note-213)[[214]](#cite_note-214) She has also won three [Teen Choice Awards](/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards "Teen Choice Awards") and one [MTV Europe Music Award](/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award "MTV Europe Music Award").[[215]](#cite_note-215)[[216]](#cite_note-216) Azalea won the [2014 ARIA Award](/wiki/ARIA_Music_Awards_of_2014 "ARIA Music Awards of 2014") for [Breakthrough Artist](/wiki/ARIA_Award_for_Breakthrough_Artist_%E2%80%93_Release "ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist – Release") and the [2015 People's Choice Award](/wiki/41st_People%27s_Choice_Awards "41st People's Choice Awards") for Favorite Hip-Hop Artist.[[217]](#cite_note-217)[[218]](#cite_note-218)

fanoutqa_005464.x:
Cabernet Sauvignon :: Wine regions :: Washington State :: chunk_0013
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Columbia_valley_cab_sauv.jpg/250px-Columbia_valley_cab_sauv.jpg)](/wiki/File:Columbia_valley_cab_sauv.jpg)

A Washington Cabernet Sauvignon from the Columbia Valley AVA

According to the Washington State Wine Commission, Cabernet Sauvignon is the most widely planted red grape variety in Washington state. It is generally found in the warmer sites of the [Columbia Valley](/wiki/Columbia_Valley_AVA "Columbia Valley AVA"). The vines are choice plantings for growers due to their hardy vine stalks and resistance to the cold winter frost that is commonplace in [Eastern Washington](/wiki/Eastern_Washington "Eastern Washington"). Washington Cabernet Sauvignon is characterized by its fruitiness and easy drinking styles that are not overly tannic.[[2]](#cite_note-Clarke_pg_47-56-2) Recent Washington [American Viticultural Areas](/wiki/American_Viticultural_Area "American Viticultural Area") (AVAs) that have seen some success with their Cabernet Sauvignons include [Red Mountain](/wiki/Red_Mountain_AVA "Red Mountain AVA"), [Walla Walla Valley](/wiki/Walla_Walla_Valley_AVA "Walla Walla Valley AVA") and parts of the [Yakima Valley AVA](/wiki/Yakima_Valley_AVA "Yakima Valley AVA") near the [Tri-Cities](/wiki/Tri-Cities,_Washington "Tri-Cities, Washington") region.[[3]](#cite_note-Goldstein_pg_134-139-3)

fanoutqa_021080.t: Flag of North Dakota :: Design and specifications :: Statute :: chunk_0001
fanoutqa_021080.x:
Flag of North Dakota :: Design and specifications :: Statute :: chunk_0001
The [North Dakota Century Code](/wiki/North_Dakota_Century_Code "North Dakota Century Code") specifies that the flag of North Dakota must:

> consist of a field of blue silk or material which will withstand the elements four feet four inches [132.08 centimeters] on the pike and five feet six inches [167.64 centimeters] on the fly, with a border of knotted yellow fringe two and one‑half inches [6.35 centimeters] wide.[[1]](#cite_note-nd‑flag‑statute-1)

The statute further specifies that:

> On each side of said flag in the center thereof, must be embroidered or stamped an eagle with outspread wings and with opened beak. The eagle must be three feet four inches [101.6 centimeters] from tip to tip of wing, and one foot ten inches [55.88 centimeters] from top of head to bottom of olive branch hereinafter described. The left foot of the eagle shall grasp a sheaf of arrows, the right foot shall grasp an olive branch showing three red berries. On the breast of the eagle must be displayed a shield, the lower part showing seven red and six white stripes placed alternately. Through the open beak of the eagle must pass a scroll bearing the words 'E Pluribus Unum'. Beneath the eagle there must be a scroll on which must be borne the words 'North Dakota'. Over the scroll carried through the eagle’s beak must be shown thirteen five‑pointed stars, the whole device being surmounted by a sunburst.[[1]](#cite_note-nd‑flag‑statute-1)

The statute continues by specifying that:

> The flag must conform in all respects as to color, form, size, and device with the regimental flag carried by the First North Dakota Infantry in the Spanish American War and Philippine Insurrection, except in the words shown on the scroll below the eagle. To ensure historical accuracy, reproductions of the flag of North Dakota must adhere to the official design and industry color chart codes provided by the state historical society.[[1]

Continent :: Etymology :: chunk_0001
From the 16th century the English noun *continent* was derived from the term *continent land*, meaning continuous or connected land[[5]](#cite_note-oed-5) and translated from the Latin *terra continens*.[[6]](#cite_note-6) The noun was used to mean "a connected or continuous tract of land" or [mainland](/wiki/Mainland "Mainland").[[5]](#cite_note-oed-5) It was not applied only to very large areas of land—in the 17th century, references were made to the *continents* (or mainlands) of the [Isle of Man](/wiki/Isle_of_Man "Isle of Man"), [Ireland](/wiki/Ireland "Ireland") and [Wales](/wiki/Wales "Wales") and in 1745 to [Sumatra](/wiki/Sumatra "Sumatra").[[5]](#cite_note-oed-5) The word *continent* was used in translating Greek and Latin writings about the three "parts" of the world, although in the original languages no word of exactly the same meaning as *continent* was used.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewis_&_Wigen,_The_Myth_of_Continents199729-7)

While *continent* was used on the one hand for relatively small areas of continuous land, on the other hand geographers again raised Herodotus's query about why a single large landmass should be divided into separate continents. In the mid-17th century, [Peter Heylin](/wiki/Peter_Heylin "Peter Heylin") wrote in his *Cosmographie* that "A Continent is a great quantity of Land, not separated by any Sea from the rest of the World, as the whole Continent of Europe, Asia, Africa." In 1727, [Ephraim Chambers](/wiki/Ephraim_Chambers "Ephraim Chambers") wrote in his *Cyclopædia,* "The world is ordinarily divided into two grand continents: the [Old](/wiki/Old_World "Old World") and the [New](/wiki/New_World "New World")." And in his 1752 atlas, [Emanuel Bowen](/wiki/Emanuel_Bowen "Emanuel Bowen") defined a continent as "a large space of dry land comprehending many countries all joined together, without any separation by water. In the 1850s, [Ferdinand Schumacher](/wiki/Ferdinand_Schumacher "Ferdinand Schumacher") and [Robert Stuart](/wiki/Robert_Stuart_(businessman) "Robert Stuart (businessman)") founded oat mills. Schumacher founded the [German Mills American Oatmeal Company](/wiki/German_Mills_American_Oatmeal_Company "German Mills American Oatmeal Company") in [Akron, Ohio](/wiki/Akron,_Ohio "Akron, Ohio"), and Stuart founded the North Star Mills in [Hearst, Ontario](/wiki/Hearst,_Ontario "Hearst, Ontario"), then part of [Rupert's Land](/wiki/Rupert%27s_Land "Rupert's Land"). In 1870, Schumacher ran his first known cereal advertisement in the *[Akron Beacon Journal](/wiki/Akron_Beacon_Journal "Akron Beacon Journal")* newspaper. In 1877, the Quaker Mill Company of Ravenna, Ohio, was founded.

According to some accounts, Quaker Mill partner Henry Seymour came up with the brand name after discovering an encyclopedia article about [Quakers](/wiki/Quakers "Quakers"). He stated that the qualities describing Quakers, such as integrity, honesty, and purity, were traits that he wanted customers to associate with the company's product. According to the company, William Heston also said that he had selected the name.[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) Quaker Mill Company held the trademark on the Quaker name. In Ravenna, Ohio, on September 4, 1877, Henry Seymour of the [Quaker Mill Company](/wiki/Quaker_Mill_Company "Quaker Mill Company") applied for the first trademark for a breakfast cereal[[3]](#cite_note-3) — "a figure of a man in 'Quaker garb'".[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2)

In 1879, John Stuart and his son Robert joined with George Douglas to form Imperial Mill and set up their operation in Chicago, Illinois. In 1881, [Henry Parsons Crowell](/wiki/Henry_Parsons_Crowell "Henry Parsons Crowell") bought the Quaker Mill Company;[[2]](#cite_note-:0-2) the following year, he launched the first national magazine advertising

Led Zeppelin :: History :: "The Biggest Band in the World": 1970–1975 :: part 01 :: chunk_0006
During the 1970s, Led Zeppelin reached new heights of commercial and critical success that made them one of the most influential groups of the era, eclipsing their earlier achievements.[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWaksman2001238-55)[[42]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWall2008-45) The band's image also changed as the members began to wear elaborate, flamboyant clothing, with Page taking the lead on the flamboyant appearance by wearing a glittering moon-and-stars outfit. Led Zeppelin changed their show by using things such as lasers, professional light shows and mirror balls.[[52]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWall2008281-56) They began travelling in a private jet airliner, a [Boeing 720](/wiki/Boeing_720 "Boeing 720") (nicknamed *[the Starship](/wiki/The_Starship "The Starship")*), rented out entire sections of hotels (including the [Continental Hyatt House](/wiki/Continental_Hyatt_House "Continental Hyatt House") in Los Angeles, known colloquially as the "Riot House"), and became the subject of frequently repeated stories of debauchery. One involved John Bonham riding a motorcycle through a rented floor of the Riot House,[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWall2008a-57) while another involved the destruction of a room in the Tokyo [Hilton](/wiki/Hilton_Hotels_%26_Resorts "Hilton Hotels & Resorts"), leading to the group being banned from that establishment for life.[[54]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilliamson200568-58) Although Led Zeppelin developed a reputation for trashing their hotel suites and throwing television sets out of the windows, some suggest that these tales have been exaggerated. According to music journalist [Chris Welch](/wiki/Chris_Welch "Chris Welch"), "[Led Zeppelin's] travels spawned many stories, but it was a myth that [they] were constantly engaged in acts of wanton destruction and lewd behaviour".[[55]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWelch199447-59)
